Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back. The players and the umpires are back in the middle. Lhuan-dre Pretorius and Reeza Hendricks to open the innings for South Africa. It will be Matt Henry with the ball for New Zealand. Here we go!
…THE RUN CHASE…

Right then, South Africa needs 181 to chase this down and claim the Tri-Series Trophy. Can they do it, or will New Zealand come hard with the ball and defend this score to get their hands on the title? We shall find out soon.  Join us in a bit for the second essay.

Lungi Ngidi is up for a chat. He says that the main thing when New Zealand were attacking was to try and keep things simple. Adds that anything pitched up was going for runs, so he changed his length and attacked the stumps to be more effective. Says that he would have taken 180, especially after the start that New Zealand got. Ends by saying that he is fine and there are no issues.

South Africa did not have the best of starts with the ball, but they did well to come back strong after the halfway mark in the game. Lungi Ngidi was the pick of the bowlers with two wickets while Senuran Muthusamy, Kwena Maphaka, and Nandre Burger took one each. South Africa have not been at their best so far with the bat but will need to play well if they are to chase 181 and claim their hands on the trophy.

A solid batting effort from the Black Caps takes them to an impressive score of 180/5 from the 20 overs. Having been asked to bat first, New Zealand got off to a flying start with Tim Seifert and Devon Conway adding 75 for the opening wicket. Conway and Rachin Ravindra carried on after the dismissal of Tim Seifert, but the wickets of Conway and Ravindra slowed down the momentum and made it hard for New Zealand to find the boundaries. Daryl Mitchell and Michael Bracewell tried hard but had to settle for 180, which at one stage looked like crossing 200.
A couple to end the innings! Pitched full, at the stumps. Daryl Mitchell lifts it toward the wide long-on region for two runs. New Zealand finish with 180/5.

Commentary.Commentary: Done with the pre-match formalities! We can see the South African players in a huddle before they spread out to take their respective field positions. Tim Seifert and Devon Conway are the two openers for New Zealand. Lungi Ngidi has the new ball in hand and is raring to go. Let's play...
The teams and match officials have lined up for the national anthems. We start with the anthem of New Zealand, followed by that of South Africa. Live action is coming shortly.

George Linde is up for a chat. He says that so far, he has batted well in the series and is happy to chip in with the ball and feels confident. Shares that they always find a way to come out better when under pressure. Closes by sharing that they have got the best team for the condition and is looking for to the final.

Pitch Report - Ed Rainsford is at the pitchside. He says that this particular pitch has had ten days of rest, and it looks like a good one, the cracks are evident as they had to manage the water content. Adds that it looks like a belter, has a mosaic look to it, and there's some live grass too, which should aid true bounce and allow the ball to come nicely onto the bat. Closes by sharing that it is a belter of a track and tailor-made for a high-quality final.

Mitchell Santner, the skipper of New Zealand, says that it looks like a good track, and they have to see what it does with the new ball and take it from there. Adds that it looks like one of the best wickets in the tournament. Shares that they have played well and but today is the final and they have to bank on the experiences of playing on this kind of pitch. Closes by adding that they have four changes with Tim Robinson, Bevon Jacobs, Ish Sodhi, and Will O'Rourke missing out.

Rassie van der Dussen, the skipper of South Africa, wins the toss and opts to bowl. He says that bowling first looks like a good option as the pitch is dry and the wicket won't change much. Adds that they are going with three quicks and two spinners. Shares that they haven't put in a complete performance and looks to play well through the 40 overs as the trophy is up for grabs.

South Africa (Playing XI) - Reeza Hendricks, Lhuan-dre Pretorius(WK), Rassie van der Dussen(C), Rubin Hermann, Dewald Brevis, George Linde, Corbin Bosch (in for Andile Simelane), Senuran Muthusamy, Nandre Burger (in for Gerald Coetzee), Kwena Maphaka, Lungi Ngidi (in for Nqabayomzi Peter).

New Zealand (Playing XI) - Tim Seifert(WK), Devon Conway (in for Tim Robinson), Rachin Ravindra, Mark Chapman, Daryl Mitchell (in for Bevon Jacobs), Michael Bracewell, Mitchell Santner(C), Zakary Foulkes, Adam Milne (in for Ish Sodhi), Matt Henry, Jacob Duffy (in for Will O'Rourke).
Toss Update - South Africa have won the toss and opted to BOWL.

There have been some bright spots in South Africa’s campaign. Rubin Hermann has impressed on his debut series, while Dewald Brevis and skipper Rassie van der Dussen have chipped in with valuable contributions. With the ball, Lungi Ngidi, Senuran Muthusamy, and George Linde have been amongst the wickets. However, the team will need to fire collectively and rise above their group-stage setbacks if they are to challenge New Zealand and claim the Tri-Series title. This promises to be a captivating showdown, where tactics, temperament, and individual brilliance could decide the champion. With momentum firmly with New Zealand and South Africa hungry for redemption, the 2025 Zimbabwe T20I Tri-Series final is set to be a thrilling finale.

The Black Caps have not only registered dominant wins over both South Africa and Zimbabwe twice each, but have also looked composed and clinical in all departments. The batting lineup, powered by the likes of Rachin Ravindra, Devon Conway, Tim Seifert, and Tim Robinson, has been in top form. Meanwhile, the bowling attack, led by Matt Henry, Jacob Duffy, and Ish Sodhi, has consistently taken wickets and applied pressure. New Zealand may look to recall a few of their first-choice players after rotating the squad in their last game against Zimbabwe. Their strategy so far has been built around restricting opponents with disciplined bowling and then chasing down targets with calculated aggression. They will be eager to maintain their unbeaten run and cap off a dominant campaign with the trophy.

Hello and welcome to our coverage of the Final in the Zimbabwe T20I Tri-Series 2025. Today’s highly anticipated clash features South Africa taking on New Zealand at the iconic Harare Sports Club. New Zealand have been the standout performer of the tournament, cruising through the group stage unbeaten. South Africa, on the other hand, have had a more turbulent journey. They enter the final with two wins, both against Zimbabwe, and two losses, both at the hands of New Zealand. The Proteas know they’ll need a markedly improved performance to overcome the Black Caps in the final.

The 2025 Zimbabwe Tri-Nation Series culminates in a highly anticipated final between two cricketing powerhouses, New Zealand and South Africa. New Zealand has been the dominant force in this tri-series, showcasing a flawless record in the group stages. They have convincingly defeated both South Africa and hosts Zimbabwe twice, demonstrating their strong form and adaptability to the Zimbabwean conditions. Their most recent victory over South Africa, a seven-wicket win where they chased down 134 with 25 balls to spare, highlighted their batting depth and efficient bowling. Tim Seifert's unbeaten 66 in that match was a standout performance, building on earlier contributions from players like Devon Conway and Ish Sodhi, who took four wickets against Zimbabwe in an earlier encounter. The Black Caps' all-round performance has instilled confidence as they head into the final. South Africa, while securing their spot in the final, has had a more mixed run. They bounced back from their initial loss to New Zealand with a crucial win against Zimbabwe, effectively eliminating the hosts from contention. Their batting has shown flashes of brilliance, particularly with Rubin Hermann's maiden international half-century and Rassie van der Dussen's consistent contributions. However, their top order has at times struggled to set imposing totals, and their bowling, while capable, will need to be at its sharpest to contain the in-form New Zealand batting lineup. New Zealand holds a clear psychological advantage, having defeated South Africa in both their previous encounters in the series. The Black Caps' bowlers have managed to restrict the Proteas effectively, and their batsmen have found ways to score freely against the South African attack. This history will undoubtedly be on the minds of both teams as they step onto the field for the biggest match of the tournament. This final promises to be a captivating contest, with both teams vying for supremacy in a crucial lead-up to future international assignments. Expect a hard-fought battle where individual brilliance and tactical acumen will play a significant role in determining the champion of the 2025 Zimbabwe Tri-Series.
